verdict.rationale: CRA's business-registration overview is written in plain, directive language a non-lawyer can follow. It says registering online is "the fastest and easiest way", lists which accounts can be registered together, points users to "Find an existing business number" if needed, and offers a separate non-resident route. However, the pack shows only overview-level prose, not explicit numbered walkthroughs, so the step-by-step depth is unproven. Missing for 10: evidence of sequenced step-by-step instructions for founder tasks, plain-language coverage beyond registration (e.g., GST/HST filing, payroll), independent or hands-on corroboration of usability.

support.subject: As a founder, the service publishes plain-language, step-by-step guidance for my task — explainers a non-lawyer can follow, not just statute text and form numbers

citations.quote: Registering online is the fastest and easiest way to get a business number (BN) and certain CRA program accounts such as GST/HST and payroll.
If you do not know your BN, go to Find an existing business number.
After registering for a BN and CRA program accounts in BRO, you can link directly to the provincial registration site.
You can register for any of the following at the same time: Business number (BN), GST/HST (RT) excluding Quebec, Payroll deductions (RP), Corporation income tax (RC)
